author: Lucy Campbell
description:
Police said they believed deceased man was assailant in domestic-related homicide at daycare center

A man killed a woman and their child inside a small in-home daycare center they own in Minnesota before taking his own life, police said on Wednesday.

Hopkins police department said in statement they responded to a report of a stabbing at the residence on the 200 block of Tyler Avenue North around 9am in the Minneapolis suburb of Hopkins. Inside, they found two adults and a child dead.

Continue reading...
title: Minnesota man killed his wife and child before dying by suicide, police say

author: Josh Taylor Technology reporter
description:
Customers will be able to pay using face and palm scans, potentially speeding up transactions – but rollout of the technology is likely to be slow

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The company behind 300,000 Eftpos terminals across Australia is hoping shoppers will want to make payments by simply glancing at a screen, as biometric technology pushes further into retailing.

Verifone is selling the innovation as “pay for
title: Pay with a glance at a screen as biometric technology company begins push into Australian retail

author: Luca Ittimani and Jonathan Barrett
description:
Investor loan applications may have fallen since the start of the year, but the slump already appears to be turning around

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Ignore the doomsday warnings about the government’s tax changes – property investing in Australia is a little bruised, but it’s far from broken.

The country’s biggest mortgage lender, Commonwealth Bank, reported a bumper $11bn full-year cash profit on Wednesday, backed by robust demand for its lending products, especially mortgages.

Continue reading...
title: Ignore the doomsdayers – property investing in Australia is far from broken

author: Martin Farrer
description:
News bargaining bill expected to pass parliament after Labor and Coalition agree on terms that will force tech companies to contribute to media outlets. Follow today’s news live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Thousands of students are expected to rally in Students Say No to Pauline Hanson protests across major cities and towns, Australian Associated Press reports.

“I’m hoping this will be the start of a real kind of movement,” said Australian National University student, Yerin Park, who is organising the Canberra protest.
title: Australia politics live: tech giants face law to pay for news content; Australia joins call for Iran to end death penalty

author: Rachel Leingang
description:
Democratic socialist Francesca Hong fell just short as David Crowley strives for unity for November’s general election

Democratic socialist Francesca Hong was on course to win the party’s nomination for Wisconsin governor on Wednesday by a clear margin, according to the polls – presaging the latest in an extraordinary wave of leftwing victories across the country, challenging the party’s establishment.

It was not to be. In a photo finish after a messy campaign, David Crowley eked out a win by a few thousand votes over Hong, raising questions over the limits of the progressive movement that has swept through Democratic contests in recent months.

Continue reading...
title: Wisconsin primary provided snapshot of Democratic party – can it now win?

author: Ashifa Kassam in Madrid, Miranda Bryant and Chris Michael in London
description:
Beginning in Russia’s remote Arctic north, the eclipse traced an arc over much of western Europe – with the best views in Spain, Iceland and Greenland

It was a moment of awe shared by millions across Europe: an eclipse that blocked out the sun, plunging parts of the continent into a daytime darkness in which temperatures dropped and birds suddenly went quiet.

Wednesday’s eclipse began in Russia’s remote Arctic north, going on to trace an arc over much of western Europe. From the UK to northern Italy, tens of millions of people turned to the sky as the light of the setting sun was almost completley blocked out.

Continue reading...
title: Cruise ships, quiet towns and an all-day festival: millions flock to eclipse viewing spots across Europe

author: Steven Morris Cornwall
description:
People came from far and wide to witness phenomenon that has thrilled humans for thousands of years

At 6pm the beach and village began to empty, and those in the know headed up the hill towards the old granite coastguard station on the headland.

“This is the best spot,” said Sennen Cove resident Lisa Redfern, who had built a pinhole camera for the eclipse out of an old Ryvita Thins box.

Continue reading...
title: ‘A magical eeriness’: Cornwall comes together for communal moment during solar eclipse

author: Guardian staff
description:
US president announced departure on social media, saying Leavitt was leaving to ‘spend more time’ with family

  • US politics – live updates

Karoline Leavitt will step down as White House press secretary at the end of August, Donald Trump announced.

The US president announced her departure on social media, saying Leavitt was leaving “so she can spend more time” with her family. She gave birth to a daughter, Viviana, in May, and returned from maternity leave last month.

Continue reading...
title: Karoline Leavitt will step down as White House press secretary, Trump says

author: Sam Levine in New York
description:
Prosecutors charge Heidi Beirich with financial crimes as part of case against the Southern Poverty Law Center

The justice department on Wednesday arrested a leading expert on far-right extremism, charging her with financial crimes as part of the government’s ongoing case against the Southern Poverty Law Center (SPLC).

Federal prosecutors charged Heidi Beirich, who formerly served as the group’s chief financial officer, with conspiracy to commit wire fraud, conspiracy to submit false statements to a federally insured bank and conspiracy to commit concealment money laundering.

Continue reading...
title: Trump’s justice department arrests expert on far right as part of SPLC crackdown

author: Geneva Abdul
description:
Kyaw Zwar Minn was ousted for declaring loyalty to Aung San Suu Kyi after 2021 coup but refused to leave his home

Myanmar’s ousted ambassador to the UK has gone on trial on trespassing charges for refusing to leave a diplomatic residence after being unceremoniously locked out of the embassy in 2021.

Shortly after Myanmar’s military seized power in 2021, triggering mass protests that spiralled into a civil war, Kyaw Zwar Minn was locked out of the embassy for declaring his loyalty to the deposed civilian leader Aung San Suu Kyi.

Continue reading...
title: Ex-Myanmar ambassador to UK on trial for trespassing in diplomatic residence

author: Tom Burgis
description:
US envoy had claimed Americans could be extracting crude by as early as next year

Greenland authorities have forced a US oil company connected to Donald Trump to postpone drilling wells in the Arctic territory, defying claims by the US president’s envoy that Americans could be extracting crude by next year.

Amid Trump’s imperialist threats, tensions have been rising on Greenland’s eastern coast after the oil company brought drilling equipment ashore in July without permission, drawing a “strong warning” from the government.

Continue reading...
title: Greenland forces Trump-linked US oil firm to delay drilling

author: Coral Murphy Marcos
description:
Kennedy Center had sued Chuck Redd for canceling Christmas Eve concert after Trump renamed institution

A superior court judge in Washington DC has ordered the Kennedy Center to pay more than $250,000 to a musician who canceled a performance at the arts center after the White House announced that Donald Trump’s name would be added to the venue.

Judge Tanya Jones Bosier ordered the Kennedy Center on Monday to pay $252,479.70 in legal fees and costs to attorneys for musician Chuck Redd within 45 days.

Continue reading...
title: Judge awards $252,480 to musician who canceled Kennedy Center performance

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Celebrity blogger was hospitalized for a mental health crisis after he harmed himself during live stream

The mother of celebrity blogger Perez Hilton is seeking temporary custody of his three children after he was hospitalized during a mental health crisis at his south Florida home last week.

Court documents filed in Miami-Dade county and seen by multiple news outlets, including Miami’s NBC 6, show the request for custody was made by 48-year-old Hilton’s mother.

Continue reading...
title: Perez Hilton’s mother files for temporary custody of his three children

author: Rachel Hall
description:
Family, friends and colleagues attend service at Buckfast Abbey, which former MP described as her ‘safe haven’

About 100 family, friends and colleagues of Ann Widdecombe have attended a funeral service for the former Conservative minister, who was killed in her home in Devon last month.

Politicians and broadcasters were among the mourners at Buckfast Abbey in Buckfastleigh, a Catholic abbey in Devon where Widdecombe regularly worshipped and which she described as her “safe haven”.

Continue reading...
title: Politicians among mourners at funeral service for Ann Widdecombe

author: Helena Horton, Deborah Solomon and Rachel Hall
description:
Amid doubling prices and fraying tempers, shoppers hunt for elusive eyewear to prepare for rare eclipse of sun

• Europe solar eclipse – latest updates

A secretive WhatsApp group was pinging with notifications throughout Wednesday, letting its members know where in London the latest “drop” would take place.

The group’s focus, rather than being for an illicit substance, was for the much-coveted eclipse glasses, which have prompted a frantic rush on shops before the celestial event.

Continue reading...
title: WhatsApp ‘drops’, price hikes and queues: scramble for solar eclipse specs

author: Sam Levin
description:
Darrell Hines’s lawyers ask supreme court to intervene, arguing he could face fate similar to failed execution in May

Tennessee is scheduled to execute a man this week despite bipartisan backlash after the state botched its previous lethal injection, which dragged on for more than an hour before it was canceled.

Darrell Hines, who was convicted of the 1985 murder of Catherine Jean Jackson Jenkins, a motel maid and mother of four, is due to be put to death on Thursday.

Continue reading...
title: Tennessee set to execute man despite botched attempt on another prisoner

author: Adam Gabbatt
description:
‘Outstanding young Americans’ came together to catch a tennis ball for freedom

The Patriot Games, held this week in Ohio, was intended to be a “national athletic competition celebrating the character, determination, and excellence that define the American spirit”, according to a press release.

The competition, which organizers insisted would be nothing like the Hunger Games, was to bring together “outstanding young Americans” from across the country, “to compete, inspire, and showcase the values that have shaped the United States for nearly 250 years”. ESPN, hosting the games, said it would “test excellence in skillsets of beloved American sports”.

Continue reading...
title: Patriot Games: Trump’s ‘freedom finale’ to celebrate 250 is … a school sports day

author: Fiona Harvey and Safeerah Ahmed
description:
PM to look at imposing restriction on devices in public spaces, though campaigners fear it does not go far enough

The government will look at banning disposable barbecues as wildfires continue to rage across the UK, Andy Burnham has said.

Disposable barbecues have been the cause of a number of serious fires over the last few years, but campaigners were critical of the prime minister’s failure to link those fires more broadly to the climate crisis.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham to consider ban on disposable barbecues as wildfires rage in UK

author: Caitlin Cassidy
description:
Managing director says guidelines will ensure no individual will ‘be the subject of comedy that is violent in its description in our programming’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A pledge by the ABC managing director, Hugh Marks, to change editorial guidelines on satire and violence after the broadcaster aired a program featuring offensive comments about Gina Rinehart, has sparked concerns about overreach.

The four-minute film, titled A Very Relaxing Video, ran on documentary-reality show Race Around the World on 12 July and sparked a furore over comments made about the bi
title: ABC changing editorial policy after Rinehart furore prompts concerns of overreach from academics and advocates

author: Achol Arok
description:
Exclusive: ‘Peaceful community rally’ of more than 150 people was walking in Broadmeadows when car travelling in same direction allegedly approached

Victorian police are investigating allegations that a car was deliberately driven at speed towards a protester taking part in an anti-racism rally in Melbourne last month.

More than 150 people gathered in the outer-north suburb of Broadmeadows on 25 July for what organisers described as a “peaceful community rally”.

Continue reading.
title: Victorian police investigate allegation a car drove deliberately at speed towards anti-racism protester

Travellers flying in and out of Sydney airport had already been dealing with heavy delays even before a Jetstar plane narrowly avoided colliding with a Qatar Airways plane on the tarmac early on Sunday.

The day before, more than 150 flights passing through Sydney were delayed as the airport grappled with a lack of air traffic controllers, highlighting how
title: What’s behind Sydney airport’s heavy delays and near-miss incident?

author: Adam Morton Climate and environment editor
description:
Proposal to cut building costs by scrapping the construction code would increase bills for the poorest households, critics say

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A Coalition plan to abolish compulsory energy standards for new homes that help reduce people’s exposure to heat and cold has been criticised by advocates as a “cost-of-living timebomb” that would deepen inequality.

The opposition’s housing and environment spokesperson, Andrew Bragg, said a Coalition government would cut the National Construction Code from more than 2,000 pages to 80, and strip away all requirements for new homes beyond demanding they were “basic and safe”. Longstanding compulsory energy and accessibility measures would become “optional extras”
title: Coalition plan to scrap energy rules for new houses condemned as ‘cost-of-living timebomb’

author: Coral Murphy Marcos
description:
Mortgage and student loan balances saw ‘small decline’ with increases elsewhere, says post alongside Fed report

Credit card debt in the United States is growing close to a record high, having crept up from $54bn to $1.26tn between April and June compared with the same period last year, according to a report by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

That figure is just shy of last year’s record high of $1.28tn.

Continue reading...
title: US credit card debt climbs to $1.26tn, nearing last year’s record high

author: Guardian Staff
description:
Thanks to the drought, these black-and-white beauties are struggling to catch worms in the rock-hard earth. But there’s still good foraging on well-watered fairways and greens

Name: Badgers.

Age: European badgers live for five to eight years in the wild. They have been in the UK, where this story is set, for half to three-quarters of a million years.

Continue reading...
title: Too many holes! Why badgers are digging up Britain’s lovingly maintained golf courses

author: Bethan McKernan Wales correspondent
description:
Investigators believe Vikings and Hells Angels members involved in violence that preceded death of Brecon man

A man was killed in what is believed to have been a violent brawl between rival motorcycle gangs in the south Wales valleys, police have said.

Anthony “Tony” Jones, 56, of Brecon, died of his injuries in hospital after the violence in Pontnewynydd, near Pontypool, last Thursday evening, which reportedly involved knives and hammers.

Continue reading...
title: Police link Welsh valleys death to biker gang rivalry

author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
description:
Labour chair says Reform deputy leader is trying to harass journalists over reporting on his financial affairs

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Richard Tice has been accused by Labour’s Bridget Phillipson of mounting a “deeply chilling attempt to silence the free press” after he sent a legal threat to the Guardian over its reporting on his financial affairs.

Lawyers for Tice, the deputy leader of Reform UK, singled out a Guardian correspondent for her journalism about a series of Tice’s financial transactions that were referred to the National Crime Agency.
title: Bridget Phillipson condemns Richard Tice’s ‘chilling attempt to silence free press’

author: Rachel Hall
description:
Sadiq Khan has indicated the technology will be deployed on London’s Oxford Street despite human rights concerns

The Metropolitan police are understood to be planning to use live facial recognition (LFR) technology on Britain’s busiest shopping street.

In June the Met said it would introduce the technology in London’s West End by Christmas and into a further six areas next year. Sadiq Khan, the London mayor, has indicated that the newly pedestrianised Oxford Street will be included.

Continue reading...
title: Live facial recognition cameras to be used on UK’s busiest shopping street

author: Helena Horton
description:
As London restaurants say wild birds are smaller and fewer this year, experts say countryside should not be ‘playground for bloodsports’

Every year on 12 August, fans of traditional British cuisine flock to plush restaurants in Mayfair to dine on grouse served with bread sauce and game chips.

But those hoping to find the small wild birds, sourced from the UK’s moorlands, may be disappointed. Wildfires have been raging on moors across the UK, burning habitats and incinerating wildlife after record-breaking heat has turned the landscape into a tinderbox.

Continue reading...
title: Inglorious Twelfth? Calls for grouse season to be banned to prevent wildfires and peatland damage

author: Martin Belam
description:
Democrats demand congressional briefing after passenger-laden Air Force One sent on decoy flight despite security scare. Plus, the 11 biggest wellness trends of 2026 so far

Good morning.

Democrats have called for a congressional briefing after a charade in which Donald Trump was secretly spirited into a different plane than the one the public and press believed he was travelling on.

How did the plot to smuggle Trump off the plane unfold? In this video, the Guardian breaks down the footage from that day, showing how the president reportedly boarded the old Air Force One jet in view of television cameras, and then was secretly shuttled minutes later to a smaller plane via an airport catering truck
title: Anger after Trump’s secret flight swap appears to offer up staff and media as decoys | First Thing

author: Sara Sneath in Palm Beach county
description:
Plans for hyperscale datacenter in Palm Beach county prompt concerns over water and electricity demands

About 16 miles (26km) south-west of Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Largo estate, near the northern edge of the Florida Everglades, developers have proposed a hyperscale datacenter on a 202-acre (82-hectare) parcel of land surrounded by water. Local environmentalists warn that the proposed 600MW datacenter in western Palm Beach county could damage the wetlands, which the federal government and the state of Florida have spent a combined $6bn to restore after decades of drainage and development.

One concern is that the datacenter could exacerbate an existing issue of toxic bacterial blooms in a water system which has already been stressed by drought, fertilizer runoff and warm water temperatures. In recent summers, the bright blooms of blue-green algae have cove
title: Heat, algae and AI: proposed datacenter could damage Everglades, experts warn

author: Michael Sainato
description:
Marni von Wilpert helped draft Protecting the Right to Organize act, and now wants work toward implementing it

Legislation that would modernize federal labor law began with a handful of lawyers meeting, of all places, in an ice-cream shop.

“We wrote for hours what we would do to amend the National Labor Relations Act,” said Marni von Wilpert, a member of the San Diego city council who was then an attorney for the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB). Bringing together “our collective experience as labor lawyers over the years, really trying to unrig the rules so that working people could have a fair shot”.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Unrig the economy for working people’: the California candidate who wrote updated labor laws

author: Hannah Al-Othman North of England Correspondent
description:
Calls for speed limiters or mandated helmet use after research into injuries at three paediatric trauma centres

The number of children involved in crashes on e-scooters has soared in recent years, with some as young as nine involved in collisions, research has found.

Researchers carried out a review of injuries among the under-16s at three specialist paediatric trauma centres – Alder Hey in Liverpool, and Sheffield and Royal Manchester children’s hospitals – between January 2019 and December 2024.

Continue reading...
title: Number of children injured in e-scooter crashes in England surges

author: Rachel Savage and agencies
description:
Operation under way to rescue dozens missing after boat overturned by waves at world’s largest manmade lake

At least 15 people have died and 27 are missing after an overcrowded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe.

The boat had a capacity of 90 people, but was carrying 114 adult passengers, five crew members and an unknown number of children, Zimbabwe’s civil protection unit (CPU) said, citing ticket sales.

Continue reading...
title: At least 15 dead after overcrowded ferry capsizes on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe

author: Maya Yang in New York
description:
With wing spans up to 3ft, the shy cownose ray species typically arrive in Long Island waters in the warmer months

Drone footage of dozens of stingrays in the ocean off New York has captivated beachgoers and marine enthusiasts, offering a rare bird’s-eye view of a species that scientists say has visited the area for decades.

The footage was captured las`t Friday off the coast of Southampton on the Long Island peninsula by Joanna Steidle, a Hamptons-based professional drone pilot known for her aerial ocean shots. It shows cownose rays gliding through the water en masse near the surface.

Continue reading...
title: Drone footage shows rare bird’s-eye view of stingrays off New York coast

author: Joanna Partridge
description:
Geopolitics and cost of living crisis have cost Europe’s largest travel company €60m so far

Holidaymakers are waiting until the last minute to book their trips because of the continuing uncertainty caused by the war in Iran and the cost of living crisis, according to Tui, Europe’s largest travel company, which said the war had cost it €60m (£51m) so far.

In the weeks after the outbreak of war at the end of February, Tui recorded a temporary drop-off in customers wanting to travel to Cyprus or Turkey, in what the company called a “volatile market”.

Continue reading...
title: Iran war and high living costs fuel last-minute holiday bookings, Tui says

author: Sandra Laville Environment correspondent
description:
Exclusive: England ‘desperately unprepared’ for effects of crisis including water shortages and heatwaves

  • UK heatwave live – latest updates

Just 20 staff are working on climate adaptation within a key government department tasked with protecting the environment and maintaining food security, a freedom of information request has revealed.

The officials make up 0.3% of staff within the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs.

Continue reading...
title: Just 20 of 6,600 Defra staff working on climate adaptation amid drought and wildfires

author: Sarah Basford Canales
description:
One Nation MP says failed WA candidate’s comments describing same-sex attraction as a mental illness are ‘highly offensive’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Barnaby Joyce has defended One Nation as “one of the gayest parties in Australia” after comments surfaced from one of its failed candidate describing same-sex attraction as a mental illness.

The former National turned One Nation MP was asked to respond to a series of homophobic comments made by a former Western Australian legislative council candidate for One Nation in a video last month, as first reported by ABC on Wednesday afternoon.
title: Barnaby Joyce claims One Nation ‘one of the gayest parties in Australia’ as former candidate’s comments surface

author: Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent
description:
Event expected to hit solar power just as fifth heatwave of summer increases use of air conditioning and fans

Great Britain faces a shortfall of electricity supplies on Wednesday evening as the near total solar eclipse is expected to wipe out solar power generation.

The government’s electricity grid operator raised an official alarm that there is currently not enough power generation expected as the moon blocks up to 95% of the sun over parts of the country, the most dramatic eclipse visible in Great Britain since 1999.

Continue reading...
title: Great Britain faces electricity supply shortfall during solar eclipse

author: Rachel Leingang
description:
Crowly pulls off last-minute victory in tight race after polls had shown his progressive opponent as a clear frontrunner

David Crowley, the Milwaukee county executive, pulled off a last-minute victory after re-entering the Wisconsin governor’s race and snagging an endorsement from Tony Evers, the outgoing governor.

The race came down to the wire, with Francesca Hong and Crowley running close to each other as each batch of results came in. Polls had shown Hong as a clear frontrunner in the race but with large chunks of voters still undecided and an ever-changing field of candidates, polling was difficult. Polls in Michigan similarly showed the progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed with a more sizeable lead than he ended up with in his victory in the Democratic primary for US senate.

Continue reading...
title: David Crowley defeats Francesca Hong to win Democratic primary for Wisconsin governor

author: Josh Butler and Tom McIlroy

title: Japanese ambassador to Australia downplays Albanese melon gaffe as Taylor claims PM has ‘stuffed up’

description:
Martin Jones expresses concern scheme will increase pressure on probation service as Burnham addresses controversy over PC Harper’s killers

Good morning. Andy Burnham is chairing a meeting of the government’s Cobra emergency committee this afternoon to discuss the heatwave and the climate crisis.

About time too, some people will say. One of them is Zack Polanski, the Green party leader, who has been calling for this and who posted this on social media in response.

Good.

Now we need action. Tax fossil fuel giants to pay for firefighting helicopters. A cool space in every community. A maximum working temperature.

Continue reading...
title: Probation chief says he’s ‘not fully confident’ service will cope with early prisoner releases – UK politics live

description:
Angus Taylor and other Coalition members not supporting shadow housing minister’s target migration numbers, which would be the lowest figures since the mid-2000s

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Liberal senator Andrew Bragg has stood by his proposal to lower net migration to 180,000 per year in a wide-ranging speech where he lamented not stopping the Morrison government’s “madness” – even as collea
title: Andrew Bragg stands by proposed migration limits – even as Liberal colleagues decline to back him in

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
Voters will be required to number at least five parties above the line in order of preference after bill passed upper house 33 votes to four

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Prominent MPs such as Georgie Purcell and other microparty members will face an uphill battle to retain their seats in Victoria’s upper house after parliament voted to abolish group voting tickets.

Victoria’s legislative
title: Victorian microparty MPs including Georgie Purcell to face re-election struggle after group voting tickets abolished

author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
description:
Exclusive: Pay increases to two weeks in England and Wales after Guardian revealed officers ‘mocked’ for taking time off

Paid paternity leave for police in England and Wales is to double, after the Guardian revealed last year that officers were “mocked and ostracised” for taking time off to spend with their babies.

The home secretary, Shabana Mahmood, has increased the amount of paid parental and adoption leave for officers from one week to two across all forces, with fathers’ leave upped to be in line with mothers’.

Continue reading...
title: Paid police paternity leave to double after fathers reported being ‘ostracised’

author: Libby Brooks
description:
In today’s newsletter: As ministers scramble to resolve overcrowding in prisons, experts say the crisis demands a rethink of who we lock up – and what happens when they’re set free

Good morning. On his family holiday last week, the prime minister, Andy Burnham, was reported to be taking daily calls from Ministry of Justice officials about his government’s early release scheme. A furious public outcry has gathered pace since it emerged that the plan – brought in by his predecessor, Keir Starmer, to alleviate overcrowding in prisons across England and Wales – might include two of the killers of PC Andrew Harper and other serious sexual offenders, including grooming gang perpetrators.

After several weeks of “system says no” briefings, which Harper’s mother Debbie Adlam has described as “a rollercoaster … really draining”, yesterday Burnham endeavoured to put a pin in
title: Wednesday briefing: Why the prison crisis is about much more than early release

author: Penry Buckley
description:
Lobbyist Jeremy Greenwood gives evidence about allegations linked to Reformers at Independent Commission Against Corruption hearing

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Members of a conservative Christian Liberal party faction received a “kickback” from consultancy payments made by the governing body for more than 600 schools in New South Wales, an inquiry has heard.

Consultant and lobbyist Jerem
title: Members of Liberal group received ‘kickbacks’ from lobbying company’s Catholic Schools NSW contract, Icac hears

author: Helena Horton
description:
Master’s student made first bar with 100% UK ingredients since 1932 to highlight affect of climate crisis on cocoa plants

The late queen was the only person in history to have ever eaten a chocolate bar made with 100% British ingredients, after she was given one as a six-year-old in 1932 by the confectioner Rowntree’s.

The bar was created from a glasshouse-grown cocoa plant, at Rowntree’s headquarters in York.

Continue reading...
title: All-British chocolate bar made by scientists using Reading-grown cocoa

author: Tom McIlroy and Penry Buckley
description:
Rio Tinto said in December it may cease operations at the Tomago aluminium smelter at the end of its current electricity supply contract

Anthony Albanese and the New South Wales premier, Chris Minns, are preparing to mount a major bailout of Australia’s largest aluminium smelter, in a deal worth as much as $2.5bn.

Resources giant Rio Tinto said in December it was contemplating ceasing operations at the Tomago aluminium smelter in NSW at the end of its current electricity supply contract.

Continue reading...
title: Massive bailout for Australia’s largest aluminium smelter expected to be announced by PM and NSW premier

author: Rachel Leingang in Minneapolis
description:
State’s Democratic lieutenant governor bests Angie Craig in another election contest pitting a progressive against a moderate

Peggy Flanagan, Minnesota’s lieutenant governor, won the Democratic primary for US Senate in the state, in another election contest that pitted a progressive against a moderate, this time with immigration issues at the center.

The US Senate race in Minnesota, in which Flanagan ousted congresswoman Angie Craig, was yet another example of progressive campaigns toppling moderates as an anti-establishment wave continues across Democratic primaries. But the state’s race was also a response to the long shadow of the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown in January.

Continue reading...
title: Progressive Peggy Flanagan sweeps Minnesota Senate primary in race defined by anti-ICE anger

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Al-Ahmed, who maintains his innocence, was accused of putting his father in a headlock in March

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The man who disarmed one of the gunmen allegedly responsible for the Bondi beach terror attack has had an assault case against him tossed out.

Ahmed al-Ahmed, 44, had been accused of putting his father in a headlock on 9 March and intimidation over an alleged incide
title: Bondi shooting hero Ahmed al-Ahmed cleared of assault charges

author: Amy Hawkins Senior China correspondent
description:
The Comac C919 will fly from Beijing to Ulaanbaatar in Mongolia, although experts say it could take generations for it to challenge the west’s dominance of the industry

China hopes to break into the world of commercial aviation with the first international flight of a Chinese-made passenger jet scheduled for Wednesday.

The Comac C919 will take off from Beijing capital international airport at 3pm, landing in Ulaanbaatar, the capital of Mongolia, just over two hours later.

Continue reading...
title: Passenger jet billed as China’s answer to Boeing and Airbus prepares to make first international flight

author: Kat Wong
description:
Officers may not have fully unzipped the bag containing the sex doll to avoid destroying evidence, one expert says

Revelations that a “body” found inside a suitcase was actually a lifelike doll may have been embarrassing for police, but experts say officers followed the correct procedure.

New South Wales police on Sunday were called to Oallen, a town near Goulburn, after two members of the public found a suitcase containing what they believed to be human remains, dumped on the side of the road.

Continue reading...
title: A ‘body’ found in a suitcase was actually a sex doll. How did NSW police get it so wrong?

Senator Darline Graham, appointed to complete the Senate term of her late brother, Lindsey Graham of South Carolina has advanced to a runoff election for the Republican nomination of the seat. It remains unclear who she will face on 25 August.
